title: p0050
universal_lens: The spatial and temporal constraints of the gridiron define a discrete state-transition system. The five-yard circle rule enforces a minimum phase-space volume, while the backward pass dictates a strict causal ordering of ball transfers, forming a directed acyclic graph of physical interactions.
gsi_mapping: GSI models the offensive formation as a high-dimensional probability distribution over potential plays. The quarterback's signals act as a hidden variable collapsing this distribution. Bayesian inference updates defensive priors based on observed end alignments (wide vs. close), minimizing expected yardage loss.
gse_mapping: GSE treats the scrimmage as a dynamic constraint satisfaction problem. The center-to-quarterback transfer is a mandatory state transition. The five-yard arc acts as a geometric boundary condition; any trajectory violating this prior to forward progression triggers an immediate regulatory veto.

primitives.name: Minimum Arc Displacement Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Also five yards apart, these lines assist the officials in limiting the play to strict observance of the rule which makes it obligatory for runners receiving the ball on direct pass from the center to circle at least five yards before progressing toward the opponents'goal.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \Delta s: path length (meters/yards), \Delta x: forward displacement (meters/yards)
primitives.assumptions: Continuous differentiable trajectory of the ball carrier; Euclidean field geometry.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs if \Delta s < 5 yards before \Delta x > 0, resulting in a regulatory penalty state.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE boundary conditions enforcing minimum phase-space traversal before goal-directed optimization.
layer2.telemetry: GPS tracking of ball carrier verifying arc length prior to positive x-axis velocity.

primitives.name: Retrograde Pass Topology
primitives.verbatim_quote: The quarter, when ready, takes the ball from his center, who passes it back between his legs, and, in turn, passes it on again, always backward for a forward pass is illegal—to the back who is selected to carry it into the enemy's country.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \vec{v}_{pass}: velocity vector of the ball relative to the line of scrimmage
primitives.assumptions: Ball position is strictly monotonic in the negative x-direction during initial transfers.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violation if the dot product of \vec{v}_{pass} and the offensive unit vector is positive prior to the snap completion.

layer2.mapping: Defines the Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of permissible ball-handling states within GSE situational reasoning.
layer2.telemetry: High-frequency positional telemetry confirming negative x-displacement of all pre-snap transfers.

primitives.name: End Alignment Variance
primitives.verbatim_quote: The side with the ball, you will note, however, has drawn its ends close in to the general formation, while ours are ranging wide.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: w_{end}: lateral width of end positioning (meters)
primitives.assumptions: Formation width is a continuous observable correlated with discrete play intent.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Information collapse if opposing formations exhibit identical variance, rendering Bayesian updates null.

layer2.mapping: Serves as the primary observable feature vector for GSI conformal prediction of offensive intent.
layer2.telemetry: Computer vision extraction of lateral coordinate variance for extremity players.
